messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the gateway/edge RFC — I want to propose we separate 'stream retry budget' from 'connection drain budget'.
Sam: +1. can you sketch the failure modes you're worried about?
Maya: Two gotchas: 1) long-lived streaming conns can exhaust tenant retry budget even when short requests need hedging. 2) during drain, we currently immediately reject new streams which kills cheap client-side hedges.
Leo: Do we have telemetry to prove that long streams are the main culprits?
Maya: We have per-route token counts but not per-stream retry-charge attribution. sample from staging shows ~30% of retry credits used by 1% of sessions.
Rachel: Proposal: maintain two counters: stream_level_retry_credits and request_level_retry_credits. stream-level is deducted only on stream aborts that cause re-origin or resume; request-level for short RPCs/hedges.
Ethan: How do we handle resume + retry semantics? if a streaming connection resumes and we replay partial tokens, do we refund stream credits?
Maya: Refunds are hard. I suggest amortizing stream credit over lifetime: allocate N credits at start (configurable by route/quantile) and decrement on aborts. No refunds on resume to keep accounting simple.
Sam: That means some long streams will hold credits without using them. Could starve hedging. Maybe make allocation dynamic: start with small credit, increase as stream accumulates latency spikes?
Leo: dynamic seems reasonable. e.g., start=1, on first transient error bump to 3, capped by route_max. Bump policy measured in error-per-window.
Rachel: Also need drain-time policy: current drain denies new streams; proposal: allow new streams if tenant_request_level_credits > reserve_threshold but deny if it would push them below. That keeps hedges alive for short requests.
Ethan: What about connection preemption? If we preempt a streaming conn to free capacity, we should try graceful handoff to the client (HTTP/2 GOAWAY or QUIC handback) before counting it as an abort charge.
Maya: Exactly. For preemption -> attempt soft-handshake: send GOAWAY with last-processed-offset and mark connection as 'handoff_candidate'. Only if client doesn't reconnect within grace window do we decrement stream-level credits.
Sam: Grace window length? 250ms seems short for mobile. 1s might be ok, but could harm capacity reclaim. make it configurable by region/route.
Leo: Need metrics: handoff_attempts, handoff_success_rate, handoff_latency, stream_abort_credit_usage. Also add traces linking original conn id -> reconnect id for audits.
Rachel: Config example for route: 
```
route: /chat/stream
stream_retry: {start_credits: 1, max_credits: 5, bump_on_error: 2, handoff_grace_ms: 1000}
request_retry: {budget_per_min: 1000}
```
Ethan: One more: telemetry tagging. We must annotate whether a decrement came from preemption, client-abort, or backend-failure. That helps tune bump rules.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: feature/stream-retry-budgets -> staging (build 4521). Tests: unit+integration. ETA 6m.
Maya: For the API surface, SDKs shouldn't need to change. This is internal gateway accounting. But we should document for customers: "during tenant drains short hedges still allowed subject to request-level budget."
Sam: Edge-case: if a tenant uses unsafe side-effect calls in streaming RPCs and we allow more hedges, risk of double-exec? need stronger idempotency checks + guidance.
Rachel: Agree. Add guard: any route with side_effect=true must have server-side idempotency token checked; otherwise no dynamic bumping.
Leo: I'll prototype the counters + tracing linkage this week. Maya, can you write a short RFC addendum outlining the handoff state machine?
Maya: Will do. I'll add a small appendix with state transitions and example timings.
Ethan: Also add a stress test in e2e to simulate 99th percentile mobile reconnects to validate handoff success rates.
Sam: Sounds good. thanks all :thumbsup:
Maya: Filed follow-up RFC: https://rwdx/notes/stream-retry-budget-addendum (draft)
